title: Preparation for General Chemistry
description: Preparation for general chemistry. Emphasis on conceptual understanding of chemical principles, quantitative problem solving, and skills needed for success in general chemistry course and laboratory.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CHEM 200.

title: Introduction to General, Organic, and Biological Chemistry
description: Concepts of general, organic, and biological chemistry necessary to understanding human biochemistry and pharmacology, including chemical bonding, stereochemistry, acidity, thermodynamics, carbohydrates, lipids, enzymes, proteins, and nucleic acids.
notes: Open only to students applying for entrance to the nursing major.

title: Introduction to General Chemistry with Laboratory
description: Survey of the fundamental chemical principles of matter, presenting students with the elementary chemical concepts used to illustrate nature and the development of modern scientific thought.
notes: This course is offered as a GE course to students in non-STEM majors and fulfills the General Education Natural Sciences and Quantitative Reasoning requirement. The course is also offered as a General Chemistry course to students in STEM majors that do not require taking Chemistry 200 (e.g. Food and Nutrition major). This course is also recommended as a preparatory course for students with limited mathematics and/or science background who plan to take higher level chemistry courses such as Chemistry 100, or students who plan to take the Chemistry Placement Exam for placement in Chemistry 200. Not open to students with credit in Chemistry 100 or 200.

title: Elementary Organic Chemistry
description: Introduction to compounds of carbon including both aliphatic and aromatic substances.
notes: Not open to students with credit in CHEM 231 or CHEM 232

title: Introductory Biochemistry
description: Fundamental principles of the chemistry of life. This course is intended primarily for majors in nutrition and related fields.
notes: Not applicable for admission to the School of Nursing.

title: Saving Our Planet with Sustainable Biochemistry
description: Highly sustainable biochemical processes such as apiary science (beekeeping), edible insects, smart textiles. Food production systems such as, aquaponics, hydroponics, and humane poultry egg production from food waste. Upon global implementation, these processes may help save our planet.

title: General Chemistry
description: General principles of chemistry with emphasis on inorganic materials.

title: General Chemistry
description: Continuation of

title: General Chemistry for Engineers
description: General principles of chemistry with emphasis on inorganic and physical chemistry and chemistry basics for engineers.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Chemical Applications of Calculus and Physics
description: Chemical problems that utilize calculus and physics relevant to upper division chemistry. Chemical rate laws, chemical thermodynamics, and molecular quantum mechanics.
notes: Recommended if a grade of C- (1.7) or below was received in MATH 150, MATH 151, MATH 252, PHYS 195, or PHYS 196.

title: Organic Chemistry
description: Properties and synthesis of organic compounds including reaction mechanisms.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Chemistry 231.

title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Properties and synthesis of organic compounds including methods of separation and purification techniques.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Chemistry 231.

title: Analytical Chemistry
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of analytical chemistry including gravimetric, volumetric, and instrumental methods.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Forensic Science
description: Techniques and case studies of mysteries solved by molecular analysis: chemical and DNA analysis of crime scenes, biochemical explanations of mysterious deaths and accidents, molecular hallmarks of forgery, chemical methods in crime deterrence, chemical causes of fires and structure failure.
notes: This course cannot be applied to the minor or major in chemistry.

title: Chemistry as a Unifying Science
description: Atomic-molecular theory of matter; use of concepts of chemistry to explain observable phenomena in everyday life, including physical properties and chemical changes; connections between chemistry and biology, earth science, and physical science.
notes: This course cannot be applied to the minor or major in chemistry.

title: Confronting Cancer
description: Humankind’s efforts to combat the diseases known as cancer. Approaches to treatment, future directions, historical perspectives and current understanding through the lenses of medicine, science, and society.
notes: This course cannnot be applied to the minor or major in chemistry.

title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
description: Basic concepts of modern integrated biochemistry, cell and molecular biology.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Physical Chemistry
description: Theoretical principles of chemistry with emphasis on mathematical relations. Theory and practice in acquisition and statistical analysis of physical measurements on chemical systems.

title: Physical Chemistry
description: Theoretical principles of chemistry with emphasis on mathematical relations. Theory and practice in acquisition and statistical analysis of physical measurements on chemical systems.

title: Chemical Thermodynamics
description: Chemical thermodynamics and statistical thermodynamics, including entropy, reaction enthalpy and free energy, electrochemical processes, engines and other thermodynamic cycles.
notes: Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 711.

title: Chemical Kinetics
description: Theory of rate processes; applications of kinetics to the study of reaction mechanisms.
notes: Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 712.

title: Quantum Chemistry
description: Quantum mechanics of atomic and molecular systems; applications to chemical bonding theory.
notes: Not open to students with credit or concurrent enrollment in CHEM 713.

title: Advanced Physical Chemistry Laboratory
description: Experimental physical chemistry. Emphasis on interpretation and statistical evaluation of instrument-derived results, record keeping, report writing, and individual initiative in observing results.

title: Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
description: Laboratory course designed to introduce students to techniques used in synthesis, characterization, and manipulation of inorganic compounds and materials.

description: Application of instrumental methods of chemical separations and analysis frequently used in all disciplines of chemistry.

notes: See

description: Individual laboratory investigation.

title: Senior Project
description: Individual literature and/or laboratory investigation and report on a problem.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Advanced Physical Chemistry
description: Problems in chemical thermodynamics, statistical mechanics, chemical kinetics, quantum chemistry and molecular structure and spectroscopy, with applications.

title: Computational Chemistry
description: Theory and practice of computational methods applied to chemical problems, including electronic structure calculations, Monte Carlo methods, molecular dynamics simulations, and reaction modeling.

title: Inorganic Chemistry
description: Nature of chemical bond and an advanced systematic study of representative and transition elements and their compounds.

title: Inorganic Chemistry
description: Nature of chemical bond and an advanced systematic study of representative and transition elements and their compounds.

title: Physical Organic Chemistry
description: Attractive and repulsive interactions between molecules, experimental methods and applications. Kinetic and thermodynamic analysis of reaction mechanisms and noncovalent binding. Qualitative molecular orbital theory, strain and stability, structure and bonding of organic molecules.
notes: Not open for post-baccalaureate credit or to students with credit in

title: Synthetic Organic Chemistry
description: Modern methods, strategies, and mechanisms in advanced organic synthesis. Retrosynthetic analysis of and synthetic routes towards biologically important compounds.
notes: Not open for post-baccalaureate credit or to students with credit in

title: Organometallics
description: Advanced or special topics in organometallic chemistry and applications to organic chemistry.
notes: Not open for post-baccalaureate credit or to students with credit in

title: Spectroscopic Characterization of Organic Compounds
description: Organic compounds using physical and spectroscopic methods. Establishment of purity and yields.
notes: Not open for post-baccalaureate credit or to students with credit in

title: Instrumental Methods of Chemical Analysis
description: Theory and application of instrumental methods of chemical separation and analysis most frequently used in all disciplines of chemistry.

title: General Biochemistry
description: The structure, function, metabolism, and thermodynamic relationships of chemical entities in living systems.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Intermediary Metabolism
description: Catabolic and biosynthetic pathways of carbohydrate, lipid, amino acid, and nucleotide metabolism; TCA cycle, mitochondrial and chloroplast electron transport chains, ATP generation and their interactions and control.

title: Nucleic Acid Function and Protein Synthesis
description: DNA replication, RNA transcription, RNA processing, and protein translation, including chemical mechanisms of synthesis and cellular mechanisms of regulating gene expression; genomics, recombinant DNA, and DNA topology.

title: Epitranscriptomics
description: Advanced biochemistry of nucleic acids to include epitranscriptomics, posttranscriptional editing and modification of RNA; biosynthesis, detection and functional characterization of modified nucleotides; epitranscriptomic sequencing technology, epitranscriptomic code and its alterations in human disease.

title: Receptor Biochemistry and Protein Modification
description: Biochemical study of receptors, second messengers, and cellular proteins that participate in extracellular and intracellular communication, with focus on protein structures, post-translational modifications, and biochemical mechanisms that regulate receptors and effector enzymes.

title: Biochemistry Laboratory
description: Theory and practice of procedures used in study of life at molecular level. Includes purification and characterization of enzymes, isolation of cell components, and use of radioactive tracer techniques.

title: Topics in Environmental Chemistry
description: Fundamentals of chemistry applied to environmental problems. Chemistry of ecosystems; analysis of natural constituents and pollutants; sampling methods; transport of contaminants; regulations and public policy.

title: Advanced Special Topics in Chemistry
description: Advanced selected topics in modern chemistry.
notes: See

title: Graduate Education in Chemistry
description: Skills and knowledge needed for success in a chemistry graduate program and development as a scientist. Topics to include introduction to department research, ethics, laboratory safety, mentorship, campus resources, career planning, and effective means of finding and communicating chemical information.

title: Selected Topics in Chemistry
description: Intensive study in specific areas of chemistry.
notes: See

title: Separations Science
description: Theoretical basis for separation techniques important in analytical chemistry. Chemical and physical interactions between components of different classes of separation systems, including selection and optimization of operational parameters.

title: Mass Spectrometry
description: Theory and practice in analysis of volatile and nonvolatile organic and inorganic compounds, basic design principles, theory of ionization processes; interpretation of mass spectra.

title: Analytical Spectroscopy
description: Theory and application of atomic and molecular absorption, emission and fluorescence methods. Modern optical instrumentation and methods of analysis. Nonlinear laser spectroscopic methods in chemical analysis.

title: Advances in Bioanalytical Chemistry
description: Traditional methods such as enzyme assays, biosensors, and separations will be compared with advanced techniques including microfluidics, next-generation sequencing, and surface-based analyses. Special focus will address combinatorial library creation and high throughput screening in early-stage drug discovery using contemporary bioanalysis.

title: Biophysical Chemistry
description: Biological macromolecules to include absorption/circular dichroism/ emission spectroscopy, calorimetry, centrifugation, electrophoresis, light/small-angle x-ray/neutron scattering, mass spectrometry, and x-ray crystallography.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Disease
description: Protein dysfunction in cancer, HIV, and prion disorders. Altered catalytic function to include drug design/pharmacokinetics/ADME, global kinetics fitting software, hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry, pre-steady-state kinetics, x-ray crystallography, and structural manipulation programs.

title: Scientific Approaches to Teaching and Learning
description: Research and best practices in undergraduate teaching and learning science. Development of a teaching philosophy, discipline-based education research literature, reflective teaching practices, student assessment techniques.

title: Seminar
description: An intensive study in advanced chemistry.
notes: See

title: Research Seminar
description: Presentation of current research by students working towards M.S. degrees. Must be completed before end of second year of study.

title: Bibliography

title: Doctoral Research

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the dissertation is approved.
